items.name: HL · CRM import cleaner
items.what: Applies the Card 4 import checklist to the Growth Desk leads sheet (lowercase emails, +234 phones, domains without www., dropdown values, consent, no test or staff rows, no duplicates) and splits it into company, contact and deal import tabs plus a problems tab; the HubSpot setup itself is listed in a sticky note.
setup: Export the Growth Desk leads into a tab called Leads export with columns name, email, phone, company, website, business_type, lead_source, delivery_zone, marketing_consent, consent_date, deal_stage, weekly_value_ngn, owner, next_step_date, lost_reason, role.
Add empty tabs Import · Companies, Import · Contacts, Import · Deals and Import · Problems (n8n adds the headers on first append).
Create a Google Sheets credential, select it in every sheet node and replace YOUR_SHEET_ID.
Follow the HubSpot steps sticky note for the pipeline, properties, owners, view and dashboard.
items.test: Put 12 rows in Leads export, including IG and insta sources, a www. website, a staff row and a WhatsApp contact marked consent yes with no date. Run it: sources become Instagram, the domain loses www., the staff row and the consent are listed in Import · Problems, and the first 10 people are marked batch 1.

walk.title: Build it: a clean import for Harvest Lane's first CRM
walk.sample: 12 rows in Leads export · sources IG and insta · www.bodijasuites.example · a staff row · a WhatsApp contact marked consent yes with no date

steps.say: The CRM itself is set up in HubSpot's screens, after Tolu agrees a one-page design: five stages with exit rules, at most ten custom properties, owners Tolu and Bisi. This helper makes the import clean.
show: Proposal sent 50% · Trial order 75% · Won / Lost

steps.say: We run it by hand when the leads export is ready. It sends nothing and changes nothing in HubSpot.
We read the leads exported from Growth Desk, one row per person, with the company's website in its own column.
show: name, email, phone, company, website, lead_source…

steps.say: First, test rows, staff and suppliers come out, and a repeated email is caught. HubSpot matches contacts on email, so duplicates start here.
Emails go lowercase, phones become plus two three four, and websites lose the www, because HubSpot matches companies on domain. Otherwise Bodija Suites becomes three companies.
Sources and business types must match the dropdown values. IG, insta and Instagram ad all become Instagram, so the report shows one source, not four.
Consent travels with the record. Yes without a date becomes unknown, because a WhatsApp contact is not consent to email.
show: consent yes + no date → unknown + problem

steps.say: Deals must use one of the five stages, and every open deal needs an owner and a next step date. A lost deal needs a reason.
show: open deal: owner Tolu or Bisi

steps.say: The first ten people are marked batch one. Import those, check the associations, then the rest.
Each record goes to its own tab: company, contact, deal, or problem.
Import companies first, so contacts can be matched to them by domain.
Then contacts, linked to their company by domain, then open deals. Check that each deal shows its company and contact before importing the rest.
Problems are fixed by hand before importing. Then give every open deal an owner, save a view of deals needing a next step, and book a 20-minute Monday review with Tolu.
show: Saved view: My deals needing a next step

walk.end: Run it on your twelve rows: sources become Instagram, the domain loses its www, the staff row and the dateless consent land in Problems, and the first ten people are batch one.
